app-server-registry.title: No per-connection request serialization scopes or concurrent handler spawn; all requests dispatched strictly serially per connection
app-server-registry.rustEvidence: app-server/src/message_processor.rs:804,831-840: each request computes serialization_scope(); when Some(scope) it enqueues into request_serialization_queues keyed by (connection_id, scope) (e.g. global("config"), Thread{thread_id}); when None it tokio::spawns the handler concurrently. Scopes are declared per-method in common.rs (serialization: global("config"), thread_id(...), etc.).
app-server-registry.swiftStatus: Sources/codexd/main.swift:411-413,426-428 processes messages with `for await message in conn.incoming() { await router.handle(message, conn) }` — fully awaiting each message before the next. RequestRouter.swift has no serialization-queue or concurrent-spawn logic (grep for 'serialization'/'enqueue'/'spawn' in Supervisor returns nothing).
app-server-registry.description: Upstream runs scope-free requests concurrently and serializes only requests that share a serialization scope. The Swift port serializes every request on a connection in receive order. Because handlers (thread/start, turn/start) return quickly and run turns in the background, wire correctness is preserved, but the concurrency model differs: long-running synchronous handlers would block subsequent requests on the same connection that upstream would run in parallel.
app-server-registry.fixRecommendation: Confirm all Swift request handlers return promptly (no in-handler blocking on turn completion). If any handler can block, mirror upstream by spawning scope-free requests and serializing scoped ones; otherwise document the deliberate serial-dispatch model as acceptable for this port.

exec-unified-shell.title: Default environment policy diverges from upstream ShellEnvironmentPolicy algorithm
exec-unified-shell.rustEvidence: protocol/src/config_types.rs:218-223 Default ShellEnvironmentPolicy = { inherit: All, ignore_default_excludes: true } => by default the FULL parent env is inherited with NO scrubbing. protocol/src/shell_environment.rs:56-107 populate_env: inherit strategy (All/None/Core with UNIX_CORE_ENV_VARS = PATH,SHELL,TMPDIR,TEMP,TMP,HOME,LANG,LC_ALL,LC_CTYPE,LOGNAME,USER), default excludes are case-INSENSITIVE substring patterns *KEY*/*SECRET*/*TOKEN* applied only when ignore_default_excludes=false, then custom exclude, set overrides, include_only, then inject CODEX_THREAD_ID.
exec-unified-shell.swiftStatus: Sources/Sandbox/SpawnEnvironment.swift:24-167 SandboxEnvironmentPolicy uses a fixed allowExact list + allowPrefixes (CODEX_) gated by deny suffix/prefix/exact lists; default `.default` (:63-140) only lets through an explicit allowlist (PATH/HOME/USER/locale/etc.) and strips everything else. This is allowlist-by-default, the inverse of upstream's inherit-All default; uses suffix/prefix matching (e.g. *_KEY) not upstream's case-insensitive substring *KEY*; never injects CODEX_THREAD_ID; has no inherit/include_only/set/exclude knobs.
exec-unified-shell.description: Upstream's default leaks the full environment (deliberately) and only applies the *KEY*/*SECRET*/*TOKEN* substring filter when a non-default policy sets ignore_default_excludes=false. Swift instead always applies a restrictive allowlist. While defensible as security hardening, it is a behavioral divergence from the documented ShellEnvironmentPolicy: variables upstream would pass (e.g. arbitrary project vars, FOO_TOKEN-but-not-matching, vars containing 'key' mid-word) are dropped or kept differently, the matching semantics differ (suffix vs case-insensitive substring), and CODEX_THREAD_ID is never injected into the child env.
exec-unified-shell.fixRecommendation: Implement the upstream ShellEnvironmentPolicy/populate_env algorithm (inherit All/None/Core with the UNIX_CORE_ENV_VARS list, case-insensitive *KEY*/*SECRET*/*TOKEN* substring default-excludes gated on ignore_default_excludes, custom exclude, set, include_only, then CODEX_THREAD_ID injection) and drive scrubbing from the configured policy; if the restrictive allowlist must stay for security, make it an explicit opt-in rather than the silent default and still inject CODEX_THREAD_ID.

The Swift applier instead aborts the whole patch with targetExists. A model emitting `*** Add File:` over an existing path succeeds upstream but fails in Swift. Note the Swift PatchedFile.oldContents doc-comment even claims to carry 'overwritten content' for an Add, so the model layer expects overwrite support that the applier never reaches.

apply-patch.title: Context-mismatch error text collapses two distinct upstream messages
apply-patch.rustEvidence: apply-patch/src/lib.rs:714-718 `Failed to find context '{ctx_line}' in {path}` (change_context miss) and lib.rs:771-775 `Failed to find expected lines in {path}:\n{old_lines joined}` (old_lines miss).

apply-patch.title: Absolute paths and '..' rejected at parse, but accepted upstream
apply-patch.rustEvidence: apply-patch/src/parser.rs:729-771 test_parse_patch_accepts_relative_and_absolute_hunk_paths — absolute Delete/Update paths parse into PathBuf verbatim; resolve_path (parser.rs:84-90) resolves relative against cwd and leaves absolute as-is. Upstream relies on the sandbox boundary, not path-string rejection, and accepts absolute hunk paths. A patch with an absolute path (which gpt models occasionally emit, and which upstream resolves) fails in Swift with unsafePath. This is intentional hardening but a behavioral divergence from the audited unit; flagged so it is a conscious decision rather than an accidental incompatibility.
apply-patch.fixRecommendation: If strict upstream fidelity is required, relax validateRelativePath to allow absolute paths (resolved against root) and rely on assertContained for containment; otherwise document this as an intentional security deviation. Lower priority since the macOS sandbox provides the real boundary.

apply-patch.title: Empty-patch error differs from upstream 'No files were modified.'

persistence-rollout.title: Rollout filename embeds non-UUID ThreadId (thr_<uuid>), unparseable by upstream listing
persistence-rollout.rustEvidence: rollout/src/list.rs:930-945 parse_timestamp_uuid_from_filename: strips 'rollout-'/'.jsonl', then scans from the right for a '-' whose suffix parses as a bare Uuid (`Uuid::parse_str(&core[i+1..])`). list.rs:399 documents layout `rollout-YYYY-MM-DDThh-mm-ss-<uuid>.jsonl`. Filesystem discovery (list.rs:888-922) and find_thread_path_by_id_str depend on this.
persistence-rollout.swiftStatus: Sources/ProtocolModel/Ids.swift:9 `ThreadId.generate()` returns `thr_<uuid lowercased>`; Sources/Persistence/ThreadStore.swift:120 builds `.../rollout-<stamp>-\(id.raw).jsonl`. The `thr_` prefix means the final filename segment is `thr_5973b6c0-...` which `Uuid::parse_str` rejects, so upstream cannot parse the timestamp/uuid → the thread is skipped by every upstream filesystem scan and id lookup.
persistence-rollout.description: Upstream requires the id portion of the rollout filename to be a bare RFC-4122 UUID. Swift writes a prefixed, underscore-containing id, so any real codex-rs tool (CLI list, resume-by-id, archived discovery) scanning the shared ~/.codex/sessions tree will silently ignore Swift-created rollouts. The Swift app-server itself works because it resolves paths via its own SQLite `rollout_path` column, but the on-disk artifact is not interoperable.
persistence-rollout.fixRecommendation: Either make the rollout filename use a bare UUID segment (store the `thr_`-prefixed id only inside session_meta `id`, and derive the filename UUID separately), or change ThreadId.generate() to a bare lowercased UUID. The filename's trailing segment after `rollout-<ts>-` must satisfy Uuid::parse_str. Edit ThreadStore.swift:110-121 (rolloutPath) and/or Ids.swift:9.

persistence-rollout.title: turn_context line omits upstream-required fields (approval_policy, sandbox_policy, summary)

This defeats the very purpose the Swift comment cites for the record (resume CWD matching and previous-turn-settings recovery via reconstruct_history_from_rollout, which reads TurnContext at rollout_reconstruction.rs to populate previous_turn_settings/reference_context_item).

persistence-rollout.title: Compaction replay collapses history to a single summary message and ignores replacement_history

persistence-rollout.swiftStatus: Sources/Persistence/ThreadStore.swift:260-261 itemsFrom: `case .compacted: items = [.agentMessage(id: ItemId.generate("compact"), text: summary)]` — replaces the entire reconstructed item list with ONE agent message containing only the summary, discarding the decoded `replacementHistory` (which the reader does hydrate at Rollout.swift:887-901). turnsFrom (ThreadStore.swift:356-357) similarly appends only the summary.

This diverges from upstream context-fidelity semantics and means resumed threads have materially different model-visible history than upstream would produce from the same rollout file.
persistence-rollout.fixRecommendation: In ThreadStore.itemsFrom/turnsFrom, when a `.compacted` record carries `replacementHistory`, reset the accumulated items to that history vector (mapped to ThreadItem) and continue replaying subsequent records, instead of substituting a single agentMessage. Mirror rollout_reconstruction.rs replace-then-replay.

persistence-rollout.title: Compaction sidecar emits a non-existent EventMsg type 'auto_compacted'

EventMsg (protocol.rs:1269-1273, tag=type snake_case) has NO `auto_compacted` variant and is not #[serde(other)].

Upstream load_rollout_items will fail to deserialize the sidecar line and drop it (parse_errors++). The real compaction signal (the `compacted` RolloutItem line) is emitted faithfully, so this sidecar is purely additive noise, but it is not a real upstream wire type and the extra fields (phase/reason/tokens_*) have no upstream analog on that event.
persistence-rollout.fixRecommendation: Either drop the sidecar entirely (the `compacted` RolloutItem already records compaction) or change the sidecar to the upstream-valid `{type:"context_compacted"}` unit event. Edit Rollout.swift:424-441.

persistence-rollout.title: Native (non-Rust-shaped) rollout lines are unreadable by upstream for structured item types

For a frontend that only talks to the Swift app-server this is fine (Swift reads its own native lines), but the rollout file is not a faithful reproduction of upstream's model-visible history for these item types, breaking cross-impl resume fidelity of tool/exec history.
persistence-rollout.fixRecommendation: If cross-impl rollout interop is a goal, extend threadItemToResponseItem + rustRolloutLine to emit commandExecution/fileChange as the upstream FunctionCall/LocalShellCall/CustomToolCallOutput response_item shapes. Otherwise document that Swift rollouts are not upstream-replayable for these item types.

persistence-rollout.title: session_meta omits forked_from_id and uses non-upstream originator/source identifiers
persistence-rollout.rustEvidence: rollout/src/recorder.rs (RolloutRecorderParams::Create) and protocol.rs:2720-2751 SessionMeta: `forked_from_id` (skip_if_none) is written for forked threads; `originator` comes from default_client originator (e.g. codex_cli_rs); default `source` is VSCode but the app-server path maps app-server→Mcp (protocol.rs:2624 from_startup_arg: 'mcp'|'appserver'|'app-server'|'app_server' => Mcp).

The originator/source values are Swift-specific and differ from real codex identifiers; source `vscode` for an app-server host diverges from upstream's `mcp` mapping. These are tolerated by deserializers (extra/missing optionals) but are not faithful values.

Consider plumbing a real per-host source (mcp for app-server) and an originator override rather than the hardcoded codex-swift string.

config.title: config/read.config returns raw merged TOML instead of the typed v2 Config projection
config.rustEvidence: app-server/src/config_manager_service.rs:127-139 — `let effective = layers.effective_config(); let effective_config_toml: ConfigToml = effective.try_into()?; let json_value = serde_json::to_value(&effective_config_toml)?; let config: ApiConfig = serde_json::from_value(json_value)?` where ApiConfig = codex_app_server_protocol::Config (config.rs:246-285). The v2 Config struct fields (model, review_model, model_context_window, model_auto_compact_token_limit, model_provider, approval_policy, sandbox_mode, sandbox_workspace_write, web_search, profile, instructions, developer_instructions, compact_prompt, service_tier, analytics, …) have NO skip_serializing_if, so absent values serialize as explicit `null`. ConfigToml has no `#[serde(flatten)] additional`, so unknown TOML keys are DROPPED during `try_into::<ConfigToml>()`.
config.swiftStatus: Sources/Config/Config.swift:214 `func configObjectJSON() -> [String: ConfigValue] { merged }`; RequestRouter.swift:1745 `var configJSON = effectiveConfig.configObjectJSON().mapValues(toJSON)`. Swift emits the raw deep-merged map: it includes arbitrary unknown keys upstream would drop, and omits known-but-unset fields (e.g. model/review_model/sandbox_workspace_write are simply absent rather than `null`).
config.description: Upstream config/read.config is a strongly-typed projection: every known ConfigToml field appears (null when unset) and any non-schema key is stripped. Swift returns the raw merged TOML, so the field set and null-vs-absent semantics differ. A client that reads typed fields (e.g. config.model === null vs undefined) or that does not expect extra keys sees a different shape.
config.fixRecommendation: In RequestRouter config/read handling, build the response `config` by projecting the merged map onto the known v2 Config field list: emit each known snake_case field with its merged value or explicit `.null`, and drop keys not in the v2 Config schema (preserving the `additional`-flatten keys upstream keeps only after ConfigToml round-trips, i.e. none of the unknown top-level keys). Add a ConfigToml field whitelist mirroring config_toml.rs ConfigToml + v2 Config.

config.title: config/read.layers emitted in wrong order and with wrong membership
config.rustEvidence: app-server/src/config_manager_service.rs:141-150 — `layers: params.include_layers.then(|| layers.get_layers(ConfigLayerStackOrdering::HighestPrecedenceFirst, /*include_disabled*/ true).iter().map(|layer| layer.as_layer()).collect())`. Upstream returns layers HIGHEST precedence first and INCLUDES disabled layers; as_layer() (state.rs:170-177) emits every layer including ones with empty config tables.
config.swiftStatus: Sources/Supervisor/RequestRouter.swift:1752-1760 — layers are taken from `effectiveConfig.layers` (composed lowest-first in ConfigLoader.load(): defaults, system, toml, profile-v2, project, env, override) and emitted in that LOWEST-first order, additionally filtered by `guard let src = layer.source, !layer.values.isEmpty` which drops the synthetic defaults layer (acceptable) but also drops any real layer whose file exists yet is empty.

(Upstream also runs the matched set concurrently via FuturesUnordered while Swift runs sequentially; the ordering of the observable notifications is the wire-relevant part.)
hooks.fixRecommendation: Split fire() into a preview pass that records+emits all `started` summaries first, then runs each command, then emits all `completed` summaries — or have emitHookRuns drain in two phases (all starteds, then all completeds).

For PreToolUse/PermissionRequest, do not block on continue:false; optionally surface it via outputSchemaError to match the upstream Failed status.

context-compaction.swiftStatus: Sources/HarnessCore/SessionEngine.swift:1584-1585 emits the heads-up warning via .raw(method: "warning", params: .object(["message": .string(Compaction.headsUpWarning)])) — only a message key, no threadId. context-compaction.title: Boundary-message truncation marker differs from upstream
context-compaction.rustEvidence: build_compacted_history_with_limit (compact.rs:497) calls truncate_text(message, TruncationPolicy::Tokens(remaining)) → truncate_middle_with_token_budget (utils/string/src/truncate.rs:15) whose middle marker is format!("…{removed_count} tokens truncated…") (truncate.rs:131-137) — no surrounding newlines, unit = tokens.

context-compaction.description: The single user message that lands exactly on the COMPACT_USER_MESSAGE_MAX_TOKENS budget boundary is truncated with a different elision marker (different text, units, and newlines) than upstream. Only affects content of one boundary message in the compacted replacement history; not a structural/wire element.
context-compaction.fixRecommendation: If exact parity is desired, make Compaction.truncateToTokens emit a middle-truncation marker matching upstream ("…N tokens truncated…", token count via approx_tokens_from_byte_count of removed bytes, no surrounding newlines). context-compaction.title: insertInitialContext lacks the last-compaction-item fallback insertion point
context-compaction.rustEvidence: insert_initial_context_before_last_real_user_or_summary (compact.rs:419-464) computes insertion_index = last_real_user_index.or(last_user_or_summary_index).or(last_compaction_index), where last_compaction_index finds the last ResponseItem::Compaction / ContextCompaction so initial context is inserted before a trailing compaction item when no user/summary message exists (remote compaction may return only compaction items).
context-compaction.swiftStatus: Sources/HarnessCore/Compaction.swift:102-119 insertInitialContext only tracks lastUserOrSummary and lastRealUser; if both are nil it appends to the end. It never searches for a trailing .contextCompaction item.
context-compaction.description: When a (remote) compacted history contains no user/summary message but does contain a trailing compaction item, upstream inserts initial context BEFORE that item (keeping the compaction item last); Swift would append after it. In practice the Swift remote path (SessionEngine.swift:1485-1501) only emits .userMessage/.agentMessage and never .contextCompaction, so this fallback cannot currently trigger — latent divergence only.
context-compaction.fixRecommendation: Add a last-compaction-item fallback in insertInitialContext (search for trailing .contextCompaction and insert before it) to match upstream's three-tier insertion_index chain, hardening the function against remote outputs that carry compaction items.

context-compaction.title: ContextWindowExceeded terminal path does not fill token gauge to full
context-compaction.rustEvidence: compact.rs:223-237: when ContextWindowExceeded and turn_input_len <= 1 (cannot trim further), upstream calls sess.set_total_tokens_full(turn_context) before emitting the Error event and returning Err — setting the token-usage gauge to the full context window.
context-compaction.swiftStatus: Sources/HarnessCore/SessionEngine.swift:1394-1424: when looksContextWindow but history.count <= 1, the code falls through to return ErrorBody(message:e.message, codexErrorInfo:"ModelError") without any equivalent of set_total_tokens_full / recomputeTokenUsage-to-window. context-compaction.description: On unrecoverable context-window-exceeded during compaction, upstream pins the token-usage gauge to the context window so the UI reflects a full context; the Swift port skips this, leaving the last-reported gauge value. context-compaction.fixRecommendation: In the terminal context-window branch (history.count <= 1) of runCompactionFlow, set the token gauge to the model context window (e.g. ctx.setLastServerTotalTokens(modelContextWindow(...)) and emit tokenUsageUpdated) before returning the error, mirroring set_total_tokens_full.
